title: segfault with rightleft, keymap=hebrew & coc.nvim completion

labels.name: bug-crash
labels.description: issue reporting a crash or segfault

body:
With [coc.nvim](https://github.com/neoclide/coc.nvim), and nothing else installed, Almost always I get a crash when `rightleft` and `keymap=hebrew` are set. I've taken the effort to build Neovim with debug info and not strip the executables, see the backtrace at the end.

- `nvim --version`:
```
NVIM v0.5.0-dev
Build type: Debug
LuaJIT 2.1.0-beta3
Compilation: 
Compiled by nixbld

Features: +acl +iconv +tui
See ":help feature-compile"

   system vimrc file: "$VIM/sysinit.vim"
  fall-back for $VIM: "/nix/store/cxglgpiww68zj4qn82x3dgln8nk6zb4c-neovim-beta-unwrapped-0.5.0/share/nvim
"

Run :checkhealth for more info
"
```

To be specific, this is the nightly as of today - https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/87d892afa0475644e91d9c8a57b7c35491c4dc32 .

- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: ) behaves differently? 
  I tested Vim just a little bit and it hadn't crashed for me yet. I'll update if I'll find out it does crash.
- Operating system/version: NixOS
- Terminal name/version: Urxvt with / without tmux (EDITED)
- `$TERM`:

Crashes with both `tmux-256color` & `rxvt-unicode-256color` (EDITED)

### Steps to reproduce using a clean `nvim/` directory in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`.

```
git clone https://github.com/doronbehar/nvim-config-test nvim -b neovim-beta-crash
cat nvim/init.vim # for your own reference
env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$PWD nvim nvim/crashes.txt
```

Start type letters that trigger completion, it's probably hard without a Hebrew keyboard but I promise you that if you'll try hard enough you'll hit a crash.

~~According to my tests, it might be crucial to use rxvt-unicode + tmux with this in `~/.tmux.conf`:~~

<details><summary>(EDIT) not correct anymore, I've tested this with and without the following in `~/.tmux.conf`:</summary>

```
# Taken from https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/FAQ#cursor-shape-doesnt-change-in-tmux
if-shell '[[ $TERM =~ "rxvt" ]]' 'set -g -a terminal-overrides '"'"',*:Ss=\E[%p1%d q:Se=\E[2 q'"'"
```

</details>

### Expected behaviour

No crash.

### More info

Somewhat similar to https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/11925 (cc @Kozova1), but I hope here the issue is illustrated better. I _think_ it happens only with already opened files which contain Hebrew text, meaning you might have to open, change something, and reopen in order to trigger the crash and hence reproduce.
